title: Admission gating: runtime probe checklist and fallback obligations for experimental community models
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's model catalog is expanding with community/open model submissions. Several recent entries caused runtime regressions (OOMs, kernel regressions, degraded latency) because metadata did not capture important compatibility signals, and onboarding lacked a deterministic runtime probe and fallback policy.

Problem statement:
We need a clear, executable set of requirements and acceptance criteria for admitting new open models into the catalog when they are submitted in an unpinned or experimental state. The goal is to reduce incidents, make runtime compatibility explicit, and ensure graceful degradation when a model misbehaves in production.

Objective:
Define the admission gating contract: (1) mandatory metadata fields and compatibility signals; (2) a runtime probe checklist run by ingestion CI; (3) automated fallback obligations and pinning heuristics; (4) developer/PM acceptance criteria and rollout controls.

Non-goals:
- Do not change permanent pinning semantics for enterprise-pinned models.
- This ticket does not implement kernels or quantization changes — it defines requirements and automation hooks only.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog metadata schema contains a compatibility_signals array and explicit runtime_toggles field; ingestion rejects submissions missing required keys.

Ingestion CI runs a documented runtime_probes suite that includes: shape/IO sanity, 1-step generation latency, 128-token generation at batch sizes 1/4, KV-cache correctness smoke test, peak GPU memory trace at 512 tokens, and a quick model-size/parameter check. All probes must pass or be acknowledged with a risk waiver.
If a probe fails with memory or kernel errors, the onboarding flow must create an automatic issue in ENG with attached logs and set temporary 'hold' state in the catalog UI until triage completes.

A fallback policy exists for unpinned models: default route to 'verified-compat' variants when available; otherwise route to lower-cost-compatible variant and log a routing event. The policy must be configurable per-catalog-entry and visible in the Console.

Compatibility notes in the catalog entry must list: known hardware restrictions (e.g., CUDA toolchain min version), quantization friendliness, expected sequential/relative latency behavior, and test coverage (which probes were run).
Documentation (Confluence) includes step-by-step onboarding runbook, sample payloads, and a checklist that PMs and Solutions Engineers can follow to approve an entry.

Automated telemetry and alerts: catalog ingestion must register model-specific telemetry keys used by Console (latency_p50, latency_p95, gpu_memory_peak, kv_cache_miss_rate) and surface a pre-rollout regression alert template.

E2E smoke test: a curated small prompt set runs against the model from Canary region and must meet service-level thresholds defined in the runbook before the model is promoted from 'experimental' to 'catalog-preview'.
scope_changes: Add 'compatibility_signals' to catalog ingestion schema (backend + UI).
Build runtime_probes suite (CI job) and surface results in the ingestion dashboard.
Create Console UI affordances for per-model fallback policy and visibility of probe results.
decisions: We will require probes for every unpinned open model; waivers allowed but require PM + Eng approval.
Fallback policy defaults to 'route-to-verified-variant' if available; otherwise 'route-to-lower-cost-compatible' with telemetry label.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): finalize schema and runbook; add probes to ingestion CI.
Phase 2 (2 weeks): expose probe results in a basic ingestion dashboard and enable automatic hold on critical failures.
Phase 3 (1 week): add Console controls for fallback policy and publish runbook; train solutions engineers.
open_questions: What is the minimal probe set that balances time-to-ingest vs safety? (eng to propose runtime probe runtime budget).
Who owns the waiver process for non-blocking probe failures? (options: PM+Eng triage, Platform SRE).
Should fallback routing be retroactively applied to existing unpinned catalog entries or only new submissions?
